key_insight: Denoising diffusion models generate realistic additive-manufacturing microstructure images and enable inverse mappings from target properties or process conditions to microstructure.
engineering_relevance: These generative models could support digital-twin workflows and accelerate materials qualification by supplying realistic microstructures for computational analysis.
method: Use denoising diffusion probabilistic models to synthesize orientation-imaging micrographs.
Apply classifier-free guidance to property-to-structure and process-to-structure inverse problems.
Demonstrate a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification application.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evidence of generated-sample fidelity but does not specify dataset size, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
watch_item: Micrograph fidelity alone does not establish accurate downstream mechanical predictions; validation with physics-based models and experiments remains important.
paper_title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
